posts.title: Coyote Laughing
posts.description: cex cex “Ha ha!” The Daily Coyote In the above Nez Perce language this is a Particle form that generally describes the sound of laughing (e.g., Coyote) (see the NPD:19). Too, it is counted as onomatopoeia or as a sound symbolic expression. But, if you wish to be specific and make it referentially certain (for whatever dialogic purposes), then you may say… ʔisti céx cex “Ha ha!” This is to mean onl

posts.title: Eclipse
posts.description: Source In Nez Perce, we have the following expression (see the NPD:359) ʔipnéeculeylekse lit.: it is diving into itself “eclipse” This is quite interesting for a number of reasons, one especially is where the Nez Perce version is semantically distinct from a Western view of two separate planetary bodies where "the moon blocks the sun." Rather, "diving into itself" captures the visceral experience

posts.title: Barn Owl
posts.description: k’apk’ápno “Barn owl” Link I do not include the Latin sp. designation partly because this name is synonymous with another owl species (see the NPD, page 266).
